To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a novel member of the phob regulon was identified in the E. coli strain-specific chromosomal island and that the gene product is highly homologous with a type I secretion system of the E. fergusonii siiCA- DAsiiEAB operon.
we have identified a PhoB-regulatable gene, ecs0540, in the O157-specific region of the E. coli O157:H7 chromosome.
the ecs0541–ecs0544 gene cluster is the E. coli pho regulon gene that is homologous to E. fergusonii siiCA-DB operon.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of a novel phosphate regulon gene cluster, ecs0540-0544, in the E. coli strain O157:H7.
the characterization of the ecs0541–ecs0544 cluster, including the identification of the promoter and the characterization of the encoded proteins.
the identification and characterization of a PhoB-regulon in E. coli O 157:H7.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ecs0544 gene is a novel member of the phoregulon and the ecs0540-ecs0543 genes encode a novel RTX toxin system.
ecs0540–0544 are novel pho regulated genes in E. coli O57:H7.
this study has identified a novel pho regulation gene, ecs0540, and its operon in E. coli O 157:H7.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we identified and characterized novel PhoB-regulatd genes in the O157 strain.
the PhoB-activated ecs0540 gene encodes a putative giant protein with RTX-like repeats and that its cognate type 1 secretion system is encoded in the downstream genes, ecs0541–ecs0544.

the E. coli pho regulon is not limited to the well-characterized pho regulon gene cluster, and it is likely that the pho regulons of the E. coli O157:H7 and E. fergusoniii strains contain additional pho regulon members.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Pho regulon genes are present in a variety of E. coli strains, even in the pathogenic strains.
the pho regulons of pathogenic E. coli strains may be more complex than those of the non-pathogenic K12 derivatives.
the PhoB regulon in the E. coli K-12 strain is not identical to that in the O157 strain, and the pho regulons of E. coli and E. fergusonii are not completely homologous to each other.
